title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

details.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 Excited to share ForceHarness , an agent harness that lets frozen API frontier models understand and use wrist force for contact-rich manipulation—with zero demonstrations and zero finetuning . Why ForceHarness? Frontier models can control robots zero-shot from images, yet cameras cannot see contact forces (whether a USB plug has seated, whether a screw thread caught, which bottle is heavier, or whether a door is locked vs. merely stiff). Meanwhile, contact evolves far faster than an API call, and frozen models cannot interpret raw force streams. ForceHarness bridges this gap with two layers: Self-terminating force primitives close the fast force loop beneath the model ( search , wiggle , screw , slide , lift , ...) and stop automatically on contact events while holding safely as the model thinks. Physics translation layer converts each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty (mass, friction, stiffness, contact height, insertion advance)—with no hardcoded task thresholds. Key Highlights 3.3% → 90.0% zero-shot on a real Franka FR3 (no wrist F/T sensor) : Across 6 contact-rich tasks (USB insertion, screw driving, eggplant peeling, whiteboard wiping, bottle weight sorting, and firmness probing) using joint torques alone. Surpasses trained force-aware VLAs (200 demos/task) : Beats $\pi_{0.5}$, ForceVLA, and Diffusion Policy on both ForceBench (82.5% held-out vs. 35.3% best trained) and HiddenPhys , our new 7-task MuJoCo hidden-physics benchmark ( 96.4% / 135/140 , matching expert force controllers with 0 damaged handles ). Drop-in Agent Skill ( SKILL.md ) : Give the repo to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) and it will check force sensing capability, calibrate, and bring up your simulator or real robot arm gate by gate—never moving hardware without your confirmation. Links 🌐 Project Page & Videos : https://showlab.github.io/ForceHarness/ 💻 Code & Agent Setup Skill : https://github.com/showlab/ForceHarness 📊 HiddenPhys Dataset (1,423 expert demos, raw + LeRobot) : https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jack97/ForceHarness-Data Happy to answer any questions or hear your feedback!

details.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
details.abstract: Transformers are typically scaled by increasing their width or depth. In this work, we explore branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks, as an additional dimension for scaling LLMs.

title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation

details.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: Meet TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation Given monocular RGB video and initial 2D TCP queries, it recovers 6-DoF tool poses and gripper states. Its shared 4D representation also supports language-conditioned future action generation. We turn source-robot videos into target-robot demonstrations without recorded source states. Highlights: • 7.60 mm tracking ATE on DROID, 10 episodes few-shot transfer to UR5. • 69.19% success across 48 RoboTwin tasks. • ARX-X5 success: 30.5% → 72.0% with source + augmented data vs. augmented-only training.

details.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
details.abstract: 🤖🤝🤖 Heave-Ho: teams of humanoids collaborating on long-horizon tasks — fully decentralized, with no network communication between robots. • Low level: multi-agent post-training adds a shared residual policy on top of a frozen humanoid foundation tracking model (SONIC), so each robot handles physically coupled whole-body interaction from its own local observations. 94% success in sim vs. ≤29% for baseline and ablated controllers. • High level: a trained vision-language planner picks the next team skill, and the leader robot speaks it; followers recognize the command and execute in sync. 43/50 long-horizon trials vs. 21 for zero-shot GPT-6 (Astra), with ~120× lower per-decision latency. • Trained with just 2 identical humanoids → scales to teams of up to 10, works with a different humanoid platform (G1 + PM01), and even with people as followers or leader. • HH-Bench: 12 collaborative tasks for 2–10 humanoids, including table carry, narrow doors, L-shaped corridors, box handover, stair carry, and precise placement. Videos: https://heaveho-humanoid.github.io/

title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose

details.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
details.abstract: 🏆 IEEE ICDM 2026 Best Paper Runner-Up (Applied Track) Hello, everyone! I'm one of the authors of Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive time-series classification benchmark for non-invasive disease screening using electronic nose (eNose) sensors. Most clinical eNose studies rely on small, private datasets and random cross-validation hiding a critical real-world failure mode - sensor drift. When evaluated under realistic temporal splits, all 10 tested model families suffer a 0.05-0.12 ROC AUC drop, highlighting the gap between lab benchmarks and clinical deployment. What we are releasing for the community: S-OH Dataset (1,234 patients, 9 diagnostic groups, 17-channel time series) - https://huggingface.co/datasets/ivanpodd/S-OH Benchmark Code & Temporal Splits (10 baselines across tabular, CNN, GNN, and TS architectures) - https://github.com/ivanpodd/Breath-Dx We hope this benchmark helps build more drift-resilient models for clinical breathomics. Happy to answer any questions about the dataset or experiments!

title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion

details.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
details.abstract: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4 .

details.title: Regularized Score Centering
details.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update, even without full importance sampling (IS). Our empirical study shows that full IS produces extreme gradients and that SC significantly reduces their magnitude. However, SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback–Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner’s next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy’s next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9× the strongest baseline’s score on BabyAI.

title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?

details.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
details.abstract: TL;DR: We give an LLM agent a general self-improvement goal, a budget, and basic tools for collecting experience and editing text. We do not give it real tasks or an explicit recipe. Sufficiently capable models successfully compose their own self-improvement loops using human-recognizable learning strategies.

title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns

details.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
details.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and τ2-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces τ2-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises τ2 accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement

details.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
details.abstract: We started with a practical question: after spending many rounds improving an agent’s harness, what should we carry forward when the model or benchmark changes? The code is an obvious answer. But it often leaves out why a check was added, what a prompt change was meant to fix, or which earlier attempts failed. That history can matter when the next optimizer has to decide what to keep and what to revise. We study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI) and introduce Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) . SIM groups harness edits by the problems they address and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. The components proposing and selecting edits both read this history. New attempts extend it as optimization continues, while the task-solving model’s weights stay frozen. Our comparisons start from the same source-evolved harness, with matched target tasks, policy, optimization rounds, and candidate budgets. Across four domains, full SIM achieves higher final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation in the six cross-dataset and four Opus-to-Gemini comparisons we test. We also run ten independent coding source optimizations, each followed by paired continuations with and without SIM. SIM finishes ahead in nine pairs, with a mean gain of 2.36 score points (95% CI: 1.05–3.68; p = 0.003). The setting requires compatible execution interfaces. Most main cross-domain comparisons use one run per condition, and matching rounds does not imply equal token or runtime cost. These results support carrying optimization history into continued search; they do not guarantee improvement on every transfer. The images below show the idea and the coding results, including the negative pair. Happy to discuss the setup or hear how others preserve this kind of experience. 📄 https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18856
